sources.title: GPT-5.1: A smarter, more conversational ChatGPT
sources.evidence: November 12, 2025 release starts public rollout of GPT-5.1 Thinking and Instant in ChatGPT. It explicitly maps Thinking to the forthcoming GPT-5.1 API model and Instant to gpt-5.1-chat-latest, distinguishing both from the Auto router.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.1 for developers
sources.evidence: November 13, 2025 announcement releases GPT-5.1 in the API. It describes adaptive reasoning, optional no-reasoning mode, 24-hour prompt caching and model-generated apply_patch and shell tool calls. Hosted access is available on paid API tiers.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 model documentation (Markdown)
sources.evidence: Exact gpt-5.1 documentation binds its default to gpt-5.1-2025-11-13; lists 400,000 context, 128,000 maximum output, text/image input and text output, reasoning-token support, none/low/medium/high effort, Chat Completions and Responses endpoints, function calling, file uploads and prompt caching. Status is Deprecated; no parameter counts or full architecture are specified.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 Instant and GPT-5.1 Thinking System Card Addendum
sources.evidence: Original November 12, 2025 card identifies gpt-5.1-thinking and gpt-5.1-instant separately, describes adaptive reasoning and reports exact Thinking safety and image-input evaluation columns. It does not publish checkpoint size, active parameter counts or a full structural specification.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6. It explains caching as reusing key/value projections in Transformer attention layers and includes an exact gpt-5.1 extended-cache request. Combined with exact-model caching support, this supports a qualified broad Transformer inference, not dense/MoE structure or a complete block inventory.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses accepts PDF file inputs; for vision-capable models, the API sends extracted text and page images to the model. Chat Completions also accepts PDF file content. Applied to GPT-5.1’s documented vision, file upload and endpoint support, this establishes PDF as an API input format, not another native sensory modality.

sources.title: Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Later December 11, 2025 report includes explicitly labeled gpt-5.1-thinking comparison columns for safety, vision and other evaluations. These are performance measurements, not parameter counts or an architecture specification. The card warns that comparison values can use later versions of previously launched models.

sources.title: Reasoning Models Struggle to Control their Chains of Thought
sources.evidence: Later research evaluates GPT-5.1 among reasoning models, including a named Table 2 row. Its parameter-size experiments concern open-weight GPT-OSS and Qwen models; its 7B reinforcement-learning intervention uses Olmo. Those sizes do not describe GPT-5.1, whose total and active counts are not disclosed here.

sources.title: Sidestepping Evaluation Awareness and Anticipating Misalignment with Production Evaluations
sources.evidence: First-party research studies GPT-5.1 deployment behavior and a training-time reward bug involving superficial web-tool use. This is model-specific training evidence but does not disclose its parameter counts, dense/MoE routing or complete architecture.

sources.title: API deprecations
sources.evidence: The October 1, 2026 notice schedules gpt-5.1 and gpt-5.1-2025-11-13 API shutdown for April 1, 2027. The deprecated designation therefore does not mean this endpoint was already shut down at review time.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 3.3 and 9.1 restrict model extraction/reverse engineering and grant limited service access without transferring IP rights in the service. Together with the exact hosted release, this supports the descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open checkpoint license.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Later Table 6 explicitly includes a gpt-5.1 column, reporting HealthBench scores and response lengths. These are neither model parameters nor architecture measurements; the model-specific discussion of calculator hacking also concerns behavior rather than structure.

name.note: Official API display name; this record tracks the Thinking model, not Instant/Chat or the Auto router.

developer.note: First-party release and authored system card identify OpenAI.

family.note: Use the GPT-5.1 release family for this model and its related variants; the announcement places this iteration within the broader GPT-5 generation.

release_date.note: Earliest public GPT-5.1 Thinking rollout was November 12 in ChatGPT. The same announcement explicitly identifies its forthcoming API name as GPT-5.1. API access and the dated gpt-5.1-2025-11-13 snapshot followed November 13; the catalog records the earlier named-model release.

open_weights.note: Released through hosted ChatGPT and API access, with no public GPT-5.1 checkpoint distribution identified. The reviewed access terms grant service use rather than model ownership or an open-weight license.

license.note: Descriptive classification of hosted model/service access; not an SPDX checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: No total parameter count is disclosed in the original card, exact model documentation, later exact-model comparison columns or reviewed training/CoT research. Open-weight model sizes and benchmark or feature counts cannot be transferred to GPT-5.1. This is a bounded primary-source review, not an exhaustive absence claim.

active_parameters_b.note: No per-token active parameter count or dense/MoE routing specification is disclosed for GPT-5.1 in the reviewed primary sources. Reasoning effort changes and adaptive thinking time do not establish a parameter count.

architecture.note: Qualified operational inference: exact GPT-5.1 launch and documentation support prompt caching, and the pre-GPT-5.6 technical guide includes gpt-5.1 while explaining attention-layer key/value caching in Transformer layers. This establishes broad Transformer-based attention, not exclusively Transformer blocks, dense/MoE routing, dimensions or a complete architecture specification.

context_window.note: Exact API model documentation lists a 400,000-token context window and separately 128,000 maximum output tokens. These are API specifications; do not add the two or substitute ChatGPT product limits.

modalities.note: Exact model supports text/image input and text output. PDF denotes the documented API file path that extracts text and page images for a vision model; it does not assert native PDF sensing, audio input or audio output.

reasoning.note: GPT-5.1 Thinking/API supports reasoning tokens and configurable low/medium/high effort. The default none setting disables reasoning for a request; it does not make this a non-reasoning-only model.

tool_call.note: Exact model documents function calling and Responses tools; original release also demonstrates model-generated apply_patch and shell calls.

description.value: GPT-5.1 reasoning model with text and image input and function calling.

patch.notes: GPT-5.1 Thinking first rolled out in ChatGPT on November 12, 2025; the API release and default gpt-5.1-2025-11-13 snapshot followed November 13. This record is separate from GPT-5.1 Instant (gpt-5.1-chat-latest) and Auto routing. API specifications are 400K context and 128K maximum output; reasoning effort supports none (default), low, medium and high. PDF input is processed into text and page images by the API. Transformer is a qualified inference from exact-model prompt caching and the documented pre-GPT-5.6 attention KV mechanism; the full block inventory, dense/MoE routing and total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed. The API model is deprecated with shutdown announced for April 1, 2027, still in the future at review time.

summary: Reviewed all 14 fields against exact-model primary evidence. Corrected earliest public release to November 12, 2025 while preserving the November 13 API milestone; normalized family, added descriptive proprietary license and API PDF input, replaced subjective copy and recorded a qualified Transformer inference. Counts remain undisclosed after original and later technical/comparison research. Context, reasoning and function calling were confirmed; API shutdown is scheduled for April 2027.
